We will use the following notation conventions for graphs.

• Labeled graphs. Denote by Kn the complete graph with vertex set [n] and edge set Un. For any graph H, let V(H) denote the vertex set of H and let E(H) denote the edge set of H. We say H is a subgraph of G, denoted by H C G, if V(H) C V(G) and E(H) C E(G). We say 4 : V(H) → V(S) is an injection, if for all (i,j) E E(H) we have (v(i), q(j)) € E(S). For H,S C Kn, denote by H NS the graph with vertex set given by V(H) NV(S) and edge set given by E(H) NE(S), and denote by SUH the graph with vertex set given by V(H) UV(S) and edge set given by E(H)U E(S). For any graph H, denote the excess of H by т(H) = |E(H)| — |V(H)|. Given u Є V(H), define Nein(u) to be the set of neighbors of u in H. For two vertices u, v € V(H), we define Dist (u, v) to be their graph distance. Denote the diameter of a connected graph H by Diam (HI) = maxu,v€v(H) DistH(u, v). • Graph isomorphisms and unlabeled graphs. Two graphs H and H' are isomorphic, denoted by HE H', if there exists a bijection п : V(H) → V(H) such that (п(u), (v)) Є E(H) if and only if (u,v) € E(H). Denote by H the isomorphism class of graphs; it is customary to refer to these isomorphic classes as unlabeled graphs. Let Aut (H) be the number of automorphisms of H (graph isomorphisms to itself). For any graph H, define Fix(H) = {u € V(H) : 4(u) = u, V> Є Aut (H)}.

• Induced subgraphs. For a graph H = (VE) and a subset A C V, define HA = (A, EA) to be the induced subgraph of H in A, where EA = {(u,v) € E : u,v € A}. Also, define H\1 = (V, E\4) to be the subgraph of H obtained by deleting all edges with both endpoints in A. Note that FAUE\A = E.

• Isolated vertices. For u € V(H), we say u is an isolated vertex of H if there is no edge in E(H) incident to u. Denote I(H) as the set of isolated vertices of H.

• Paths, self-avoiding paths and non-backtracking paths. We say a subgraph H C Kn is a path with endpoints u, v (possibly with u = v), if there exist w1,..., wm € [n] ‡ u, v such that V(H) = {u, v, w1,..., wm; and E(H) = {(u, w1), (W1, w2) ..., (Wm, v); (we allow the occurrence of multiple vertices or edges). We say H is a self-avoiding path if wo, w1,..., wm, wm+1 are distinct (where we denote wo = u and wm+1 = v), and we say H is a non-backtracking path if wi+1 ‡ wi-1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ m. Denote EndP (P) as the set of endpoints of a path P. • Cycles and independent cycles. We say a subgraph H is an m-cycle if V(H) = {v1,..., Um} and E(H) = {(v1, v2),..., (Um-1, Um), (Um, v1)}. For a subgraph K C H, we say K is an independent m-cycle of H, if K is an m-cycle and no edge in E(H) \ E(K) is incident to V(K). Denote Cm (H) as the set of independent m-cycles of H. For H C S, we define Em (S, H) to be the set of independent m-cycles in S whose vertex set is disjoint from V(H).

• Leaves. A vertex u € V(H) is called a leaf of H, if the degree of u in H is 1; denote L(H) as the set of leaves of H.

• Trees and rooted trees. We say a graph I = (V(T), E(T)) is a tree, if T is connected and has no cycles. We say a pair (T, K(T)) is a rooted tree with root N(T), if I is a tree and K(I) E V(I). For a rooted tree I and u E V(T), we define Depr (u) = Distr (N(T), u) to be
